title: Best Time to Visit the Dooars, Month by Month
meta_description: When to visit the Dooars: winter safaris from November to March, hot April and May, the monsoon park closure from mid-June to mid-September, and October.
summary: November to March is the best time to visit the Dooars: parks are open, days are dry and 22–27 °C, and the grass is short enough to see rhinos and gaur. February and early March are the peak for sightings. October and April are good. Parks close for the monsoon from about 16 June to 15 September.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Come between November and March. The Dooars are low country, mostly 60–150 m above sea level, so winter here is not the cold of Darjeeling but a dry, mild season of clear afternoons and misty mornings. The forest department burns and cuts the tall grass in Jaldapara and Gorumara through winter, new shoots come up, and rhinos, gaur and deer come out into the open to graze. By February the grass is at its shortest and sightings are at their best.

From April the heat builds and storms arrive in the afternoons. By June the monsoon has set in, and the national parks and sanctuaries close for about three months, roughly 16 June to 15 September, for the breeding season and because the forest roads wash out. The dates are set by the forest department each year, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Winter, November to February
paras: This is the season most visitors come for, and for good reason. Days are dry and comfortable, around 25 °C in the afternoon, and the light is clear enough to see the Bhutan hills from the Jaldapara grassland and the Jayanti riverbed. Migratory ducks gather on the Teesta at Gajoldoba near Siliguri, and river birds such as plumbeous water redstarts, forktails and river lapwings work the shingle of the Jaldhaka at Jhalong and the Murti below Samsing. Hornbills move through the sal canopy at Chilapata and Buxa, and the burnt grassland in Jaldapara draws harriers and storks.

January brings fog. Mornings in the plains can be white until 9 or 10 am, which makes the first safari slot atmospheric but not always productive, and dawn temperatures drop to 8–12 °C. Open safari jeeps are cold at 6 am; a fleece, a shawl or a jacket is not optional. The fog also delays trains on the Dooars line and flights at Bagdogra, so leave slack in your plans.

Christmas week, New Year and the school holidays at the end of December fill every forest corporation lodge and most safari slots in Gorumara and Jaldapara. Book two to three months ahead for those dates, or come in the second half of January instead.

sections.heading: Spring, March to mid-June
paras: March is our favourite month. The grass is short or burnt, the sal trees are in new leaf and flower, waterholes have shrunk so animals gather at the few that remain, and the crowds of December have gone home. Gaur herds at Chapramari and rhinos in the Jaldapara grassland are easier to see now than at any other time. The Mahakal Shivaratri pilgrimage at Jayanti and the Jalpesh fair near Maynaguri fall in February or March, by the lunar calendar.

April and May are hot and humid, with days of 30–35 °C in the plains and violent pre-monsoon storms in the afternoons, called kalbaishakhi in Bengali. Early morning safaris are still rewarding, and lodges are quieter and sometimes cheaper. This is the time to stay in the hills above the plains, at Samsing, Suntalekhola or Jhalong, and come down for safaris. Parks stay open until mid-June.

sections.heading: The monsoon, mid-June to mid-September
paras: The Dooars receive some of the heaviest rain in West Bengal, often 3,000–4,000 mm a year, most of it between June and September. Rivers that are thin channels in a white bed in March fill from bank to bank. The Torsa, Jaldhaka, Murti and Jayanti can rise several metres in a night, and roads and bridges wash out. In early October 2025, extreme rain flooded Gorumara and Jaldapara, killed wildlife and closed parks for a time.

Gorumara, Jaldapara, Chapramari, Buxa and the other protected areas close to visitors from about 16 June to 15 September. Forest villages and homestays outside the core areas stay open, and the tea gardens are at their greenest, with plucking in full swing. A monsoon trip can work if you want tea country, green hills and empty roads, but it is not a wildlife trip, and you should never cross a riverbed after rain. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: October, the in-between month
paras: The parks reopen around 16 September, and by October the rain is usually easing. The forest is deep green and the grass very tall, so rhinos are harder to see than in winter, but the light after rain is clear and the hills stand out. Durga Puja, usually in October, brings the year's largest wave of Bengali holidaymakers to the Dooars: lodges, homestays and safari slots for the Puja week sell out months ahead. Before and after the Puja week, October is quieter and pleasant.

October also has practical advantages. Rooms that cost a premium at Christmas are often at normal rates in the first half of the month, the tea gardens are still plucking, and the rivers run full and clear between their banks rather than as the thin winter channels. Forest roads that were damaged in the rains may stay closed for a few weeks after reopening, so some watchtowers and safari routes open later than others. Ask at the Lataguri or Madarihat counter which routes are running before you book a slot, and check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Festivals and holidays through the year
paras: Several fairs and festivals shape the Dooars calendar, and the school and puja holidays of Bengal decide when it is crowded. Festival dates follow the lunar calendar and move by a few weeks each year.

In February or March, Maha Shivaratri draws large crowds to the Jalpesh temple near Maynaguri, about 25–30 km from Lataguri, with a fair that runs for days, and pilgrims walk from Jayanti to the Mahakal cave in Buxa Tiger Reserve. In August or September, in the month of Bhadra, tea garden communities celebrate Karam with drumming and dancing through the night, though this falls during the park closure. Durga Puja in October and the Christmas and New Year week are the two great holiday rushes, when the whole of south Bengal seems to head north. If you want quiet forest lodges and easy safari bookings, plan around these weeks rather than into them.

sections.heading: Matching the month to your trip
paras: Use these as starting points rather than rules.
list: Rhinos and gaur: February and March, when the grass is shortest; November to January as a second choice.
Birds: December to February for winter migrants on the rivers and at Gajoldoba.
Buxa Fort and Jayanti walks: November to March, when paths are dry and leeches are absent.
Families with young children: November, February and March, avoiding the cold January mornings and the Puja crowds.
Tea country and green hills: late March to May for first and second flush plucking, or the monsoon if you do not need the parks.
Lowest prices: April, May and the weeks either side of the monsoon closure, with weekdays cheaper than weekends.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit the Dooars?
faqs.a: February and March are the best months for wildlife, when the grass in Jaldapara and Gorumara is short and animals gather at the remaining waterholes. November to January are also very good, with dry, mild days, though January mornings are foggy and cold in open jeeps. Avoid mid-June to mid-September, when parks close.

faqs.q: When are Gorumara and Jaldapara closed?
faqs.a: Both close for the monsoon from about 16 June to 15 September each year, along with Chapramari, Buxa and other protected areas. Gorumara has also had a weekly closure day. The forest department sets dates each year and closes parks after floods, as in October 2025, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is October a good time for the Dooars?
faqs.a: Yes, with two cautions. The parks reopen in mid-September and October is green and pleasant, but the grass is tall, so rhinos are harder to spot than in winter. Durga Puja week brings huge crowds and full lodges; book months ahead or avoid it. Rain can linger into early October.

faqs.q: How cold does it get in the Dooars in winter?
faqs.a: Not very, by hill standards. Afternoons are around 22–27 °C, but dawn temperatures in January fall to 8–12 °C in Lataguri and Madarihat, and colder in Samsing. Open safari jeeps at 6 am feel much colder, so bring a fleece or jacket, a cap and a shawl for early slots.

faqs.q: Can we visit the Dooars during the monsoon?
faqs.a: You can visit the villages and tea gardens, but not the national parks, which close from about 16 June to 15 September. Rain is heavy, rivers rise quickly and roads wash out. Stay in Samsing, Jhalong or a tea garden homestay, keep plans flexible and never cross a riverbed after rain.

faqs.q: Is April too hot for a Dooars trip?
faqs.a: April is warm but workable: days of 30–33 °C in the plains, afternoon storms and cool mornings for safaris. May is hotter and more humid. Take the earliest safari slot, rest at midday and consider sleeping at Samsing or Suntalekhola, which are a few degrees cooler, and coming down for safaris.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see rhinos in Jaldapara?
faqs.a: February to April, after the grass has been burnt or cut and new shoots draw rhinos into the open. The first morning slot is best, when they graze before the heat. November to January also gives good chances, though the grass is taller in November.

faqs.q: When should we avoid the Dooars because of crowds?
faqs.a: Durga Puja week in October, Christmas to New Year and long weekends in winter, when Bengali families fill lodges and safari slots sell out. If you must travel then, book two to three months ahead. The second half of January and most of March are quieter and just as good for wildlife.

faqs.q: What should we pack for a winter safari in the Dooars?
faqs.a: A warm fleece or jacket and a cap for 6 am jeep rides, muted clothing in green, brown or grey, a scarf against dust, binoculars, sunscreen for midday and comfortable shoes. Carry the ID used for the safari booking. Mosquito repellent helps at dusk, even in winter.
